propositions: Compaction fold mutates worktree before git commit with no rollback on worker death, leaving dirty tree that breaks sync merge and strands local commits.
Tracked runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) committed before gitignore patterns exist cause persistent tracked dirt in every git status check.
Sync reconverge fails on both untracked-file collisions and tracked-file deletions/modifications during merge, leaving tickets wedged and store unavailable.
Store-wide fsck and compact scans have no scoping to active tickets, causing quadratic cost growth as archived ticket volume increases.
fsck and doctor repair lack detection and recovery logic for dirty-tree, stale-lock, and orphaned marker residue classes.
Push recovery path missing the same untracked-collision and tracked-deletion recovery as sync reconverge, creating asymmetric failure modes.
